settings.parameter_basis: USGS1995 N2 heat functions and historicalR preserved. Molecular mass and nominal LJ diameter from existing source pack. All geometry, viscosity, surface tension, heat capacities/conductances and boundary programmes are virtual inputs, not the Wadsworth specimen or realbrick. No transfer of glass fit coefficients.
settings.scope: Finite ideal-N2 exchange between a deforming viscous spherical pore and a rigid gas reservoir, each with lumped body heat storage. USGS1995 gas reference, constant virtual matrix coefficients, molecular effusion port. No reaction, pore connectivity law, solid thermal expansion or real-brick qualification.

connection.interpretation: Ideal zero-thickness ballistic port with negligible area relative to the spherical cavity. Port traction and rim energy perturbations are omitted, so spherical mechanics is a declared leading-order lumped approximation.

sources.title: Cavitation and Bubble Dynamics
sources.use: Full Rayleigh-Plesset surface traction and closed ideal-gas pressure; creeping infinite-matrix limit derived separately.
Vented spherical-shell porosity law only; experimental glass viscosity and glass-bead qualification not transferred to brick.

mechanical_source.selected_model: Finite spherical incompressible Newtonian shell, fixed matrix volume, outer normal traction -p_out, no exterior surface energy, constantT and gamma; closed ideal gas or prescribed pressure venting.
literal_source_cautions: Wadsworthp5prose describeszero porosityat infinite time, but its Eq2.12 has an integrable phi^(-2/3) closure time for constant finite positive viscosity. Distinguish prose from the equation actually used.
Wadsworthp8viscosity prose writes mu=A+B/(T-C); no logarithm is printed while p9figure uses viscosity of10^5to10^13Pa*s. No empirical viscosity parameter admitted until original2014source is checked.

additional_visual_review.scope: Confirmed the literal viscosity expression without log and material/method statements; empirical fit remains unadmitted.

wadsworth2014.reviewed: Publisher fulltext HTML section3 Table2; PDF download not obtained.
wadsworth2014.basis: Glass-bead viscosity is predicted using Fluegel2007; DGG is a separate viscosity standard. Do not interchange these materials.

fluegel2007.title: Glass viscosity calculation based on a global statistical modelling approach
fluegel2007.temperature_policy: Isokom temperatures in the composition regression are Celsius; Celsius/Kelvin conversion requires the same shift of fitted T0.
fluegel2007.classification: Empirical composition-viscosity model; not a physical law or target-brick viscosity measurement.

unresolved: 2016 printed viscosity equation omits logarithm. Primary Fluegel2007 supports logarithmic form, but the2016 literal expression is retained as a source discrepancy.
2014 glass-bead A=-2.6387 andC=530.754 differ from2016 A=-2.63 andC=530.60. No silent replacement or mixing.
No target-brick viscosity applicability or uncertainty demonstrated.

thermal_source.scope: Pure reference graphite and ideal gases; not measured sludge char, finite reaction rate, volatile inventory, or actual brick atmosphere.

effusion.locator: PDFpage2 Eqs3-5; page3 Eqs13/20/21. Page3 visually checked.
effusion.source_scope: Monatomic ideal-gas effusion; mean translational crossing energy2kBT. Polyatomic internal energy below is a separately derived local-equilibrium extension, not asserted as a result of that paper.

thermal_pressure_ratio.locator: Eqs5.284-5.286; held-temperature mass-stationary state, not isolated thermal equilibrium

effusion_source.internal_mode_extension: Internal mode energy is statistically independent of center-of-mass speed in an equilibrated ideal gas. Crossing energy is bulku-3RT/2+2RT=h-RT/2. No reaction, adsorption or velocity-selective membrane.
effusion_source.physical_scope: Reservoirs internally equilibrated; molecular mean free path far exceeds zero-thickness aperture diameter. No finite-length pore geometry, intermolecular collision correction, continuum advection, radiative/wall conduction, reaction or brick validation.

molecular_source.scope: Pure dilute-gas viscosity and first-order binary molecular diffusion only; explicit zero-dipole LJ approximation. No mixture-viscosity, porous effective diffusivity, Darcy permeability, multicomponent flux, Soret or brick qualification. GRI NASA thermo and reactions are not imported. No post-fit calibration to NIST tables. NIST comparison pressure is unspecified on selected pages; agreement is not pressure-matched experimental validation.
